title: Mort - I'm making a grim bullet heaven pixel roguelike where your lantern is a sarcastic ghost who doesn't remember dying.
author: cammo328
selftext: I've been creating this dark horde-slaying bullet heaven for a few weeks now and would love to get some play-testers if anyone is interested. Unlock new heroes, transformations for those heroes, unique skill combinations called requiems, and more.

comments.author: NoBackupDev
comments.body: Very interesting art style. Curious how you achieved this. Did you have a target in mind?

replies.author: cammo328
replies.body:
Yes I did. This is also my first experience working with Claude or AI in general, and I’m probably well over 500 prompts in this project. I was pretty specific on wanting to create a grim 2.5d art style where we create sprites that can read well enough in a game like this, but not need the all out detail of a 3d model. So far, in my short experience, detailed 3d models to really achieve the look you want are pretty challenging. I also wanted 2.5d so that the light(Mort) would still bounce off of the assets and give it a deeper feel than just 2d.  
It was a lot of back and forth with Claude, and a lot of tweaks, but it made an asset generator which used my GPU, that stuck to this specific theme and flavor, and was able to create images off of a thorough description, which turned into a 3d model(where a lot of the details weren’t really great), and then off of that model create an 8-directional sprite sheet. I had it build a ton of other options in the generator like characters holding certain weapons, recoloring sprites, enemies having glowing eyes in the dark, etc.  
Hope this provided some insight! Let me know if you want any more info
